correctness.rationale: Subtracting the unnormalized heat equations on a spoke contributes −mg_i+z and the within-periphery generator with rates c_ij−1; the bridge difference receives the sum of the 2(m−1) oriented spoke gradients minus 2z. The gradient system is irreducible with nonnegative off-diagonal entries even when m=2. Its positive exponential bounds spoke and bridge magnitudes by the ordered solutions a(t), b(t) with a(0)=b(0)=1. In particular (b−a)'=(3m−5)a−3(b−a), giving b>a at t>0. Peripheral differences obey the claimed e^(−mt) bound because the periphery forcing is constant and the remaining Markov evolution contracts oscillation. The bridge satisfies b'>−2b, so this bound is strictly below b at positive time. The unit ramp attains b, and equality against the strictly positive bridge row forces all initially oriented tree-edge differences to have the same sign and unit magnitude. The two-dimensional system has characteristic polynomial ξ²−(m+2)ξ+2 for minus its matrix, and b'(0)=2m−4. This gives the printed coefficients, with β<m+2≤3m−2 and hence B>0. The derivative has at most one zero and contracts strictly for m=2 at positive time. For m≥3, the peak ratio is m²/3 times 1+O(1/m); A=3−8/m+O(m^(−2)) and α=O(1/m) give the two stated expansions. Positive heat averaging of the norm-attaining ramp implies strict norm below the diameter bound 3 at finite positive time; t=0 has norm one.

evidence: Write L=L_D+P with D the older double star, d=m−1, and P the within-periphery heat Laplacian on both sides, zero at hubs. The tree Laplacian acts as identity on each mean-zero leaf space and preserves the complementary constant-periphery space, on which P is zero. Hence L_D commutes with P and H_t=T_t exp(−tP). The latter averages each leaf block and fixes the hubs, contracting the tree Lipschitz norm, which is bounded by the clique norm. Thus old bridge/spoke bounds transfer with strict spoke dominance.

For leaf pairs within one side, T_t multiplies differences by e^(−t). Split P into the unit complete-graph Laplacian and a nonnegative extra-rate Laplacian; they commute because the first acts as (m−1)I on contrasts and zero on constants. The extra-rate heat contracts oscillation, so the new metric edges are bounded by e^(−mt). The older bridge norm is strictly greater than e^(−2t), by the positive two-mode bridge system (or its positive return term and positive leaf coupling).

The older ramp is fixed by exp(−tP); it attains the same norm. Older bridge-row positivity forces a common-sign saturated tree gradient for the smoothed input, hence only the ramp modulo constants and scaling. Invertibility and fixation of the ramp and constants transfer uniqueness to the original input. Peak and asymptotics then follow from the identical explicit profile; its printed peak-time error is a direct expansion of that formula.
